morgan: Quick heads-up — ran into a streaming edgecase in the py SDK.

morgan: Repro (minimal):
```py
# using client.stream_chat() API
async for chunk in client.stream_chat(...):
    if some_condition:
        break  # early exit
# socket stays open, process keeps fd until GC
```

morgan: If you don't fully drain/close the iterator the socket remains. On long lived apps this eventually exhausts fds.

julia: oof. do you have a reproducible script?

morgan: yes — will paste gist in a sec. It's intermittent unless client is idle for ~30s, then cancel + exit path doesn't run finalizer. Looks like generator finalizer never runs when coroutine cancelled during chunk receive.

kevin: this sounds like the `async generator aclose()` ordering issue we've seen. Are you using typed signature like `-> AsyncIterator[TokenChunk]`? mypy sometimes forces me to wrap in `Generator[... , None, None]` hacks.

morgan: yup typing might be part of it. Example snippet: `async def stream_chat(...) -> AsyncIterator[str]:` then using `async for` works, but the library's `__aiter__` wrapper returns a proxy object that doesn't implement `aclose` correctly.

julia: can you try explicitly calling `await stream.aclose()` in except/finally to see if that fixes? if it does, we can treat as a bug in wrapper.

morgan: confirmed: adding `try/finally: await it.aclose()` cleans fd immediately. But users expect `break` to close.

kevin: workaround idea: add a `__anexit__`/context-manager helper in the SDK so sample apps can do `async with client.stream_chat(...) as it:` and that will guarantee close on exit. Also patch docs.

julia: agree. long-term we should fix wrapper to forward `aclose` and implement proper finalizer. Short-term add a sample in onboarding docs and mention the `async with` pattern.

morgan: another small annoyance: mypy flags `async def foo() -> AsyncIterator[dict]` when we yield `bytes` chunks as `-> AsyncIterator[Union[str, bytes]]`. Users get confused. We should document the chunk types and add TypedDict for chunk shapes.

kevin: opened a tracking issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1427 (stream iterator cancellation + typing). added repro and suggested workaround. @devex-bot can you add label "streaming" and assign to eng-ml?

devex-bot: label "streaming" added to issue #1427. Assigned to eng-ml.

morgan: for the sample app (onboarding) we should change the streaming quickstart to use the `async with` pattern and show `try/finally` snippet as defensive code. It's low friction and prevents new users hitting fd leaks.

julia: also add a small unit test that simulates cancellation at mid-chunk (use `asyncio.CancelledError` injection) so CI catches regressions.

kevin: FYI the kernel selection doc for callbacks mentions that streaming frames can be binary or text. I'll add a short table to clarify. That should help mypy and JS/Python parity docs.

morgan: pinging @kevin and @julia — I can open a tiny PR that: (1) updates quickstart sample to `async with`, (2) adds `await it.aclose()` example in advanced section, (3) adds a typing note for chunk union types.

julia: please do. also add an integration test in `sample-apps/echo` to reproduce the fd leak. CI should fail on file descriptor growth threshold.

kevin: one more thought: maybe default client should set a soft idle timeout that auto-closes if iterator isn't polled for N seconds. But that could surprise users. Put behind opt-in flag for now.

morgan: agreed, opt-in for now. I'll file a follow-up RFC.

sre-bot: FYI incident #2029 (fd-exhaustion in staging) referenced this pattern. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2029

morgan: thanks — pushing PR now with tests + docs. will tag reviewers. :rocket:

julia: thank you — huge QoL improvement for onboarding. :clap:

kevin: leaving a note to maintainers: check `__aiter__` wrapper in `client/_streaming.py` — seems to lose `aclose` binding when wrapping generator in proxy.

morgan: noted. I'll add that to the PR description.

morgan: later update: PR #2015 opened. includes sample change and repro test.

devex-bot: PR #2015 created by morgan and linked to issue #1427.

morgan: closing thread, follow discussions in the PR for details.
